lesson.menu_desc: A closing checklist with ten items and nobody doing all ten — causative have and get something done
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 4 -- Getting Things Done Through Others
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Samuel Rodrigues | Lesson 4 -- The Grammar of Delegation
lesson.grammar_point: causative have and get something done

listenings.text: Samuel, this is Karl Ellsworth, I am general counsel at Brightmoor Capital. We are the foreign landlord on the Pinheiros lease and we go to signing in eleven days. I want to be very clear about what I expect before then. We are having the title searched by our own firm in Sao Paulo, and we have already had the property appraised. What I need from your side is the due diligence report, confirmation that the lien on the parking structure has been discharged, and a counsel opinion letter on signing authority. I would also like to have the novation agreement reviewed before it goes into escrow, because the tenant assigned the original lease last year and I am not comfortable with the assignment language. Send me a timeline today, please, with who is doing what.

Samuel, Diane. I read your draft reply to Karl and there is one thing to fix before you send it. You wrote that you will review the novation agreement, you will search the title, you will discharge the lien. All in the first person, all yourself. That is not how a senior lawyer answers a general counsel, and it is not even true. Say what you will have done, and by whom. We will have the novation agreement reviewed by our banking team. We are having the lien discharge confirmed by the registry this week. The structure does two things for you. It shows you are coordinating a transaction rather than doing tasks, and it protects you, because you are not personally promising work that another team delivers. Same facts, different register.

matching.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: the day the deal is signed and the money moves
the investigation you run before you commit
a promise in a contract to do or not do something
any claim or restriction attached to an asset
replacing one party in a contract with a new one, with everyone's consent
an expert's statement of what something is worth
a creditor's hold on an asset until a debt is paid
money held by a third party until the conditions are met

items.situation: The client asks who is checking the title. Answer with the causative, not the first person.
tips: We are having the title searched by our office in Sao Paulo.
We will have the title searched before the end of the week.

items.situation: He asks about the novation agreement. Recommend a step, in a professional register.
tips: I'd recommend having the novation agreement reviewed by our banking team first.
The standard practice is to have these clauses verified by outside counsel.

items.situation: Something is already finished. Say it, without saying you did it yourself.
tips: We have already had the property appraised.
The lien discharge has been confirmed by the registry.

items.situation: He wants it faster than you can deliver. Push back, politely, and give a date.
tips: I'd push back slightly on that timeline: due diligence takes five working days.
I can have the report carried out by Thursday, not Tuesday.

items.situation: Close the call: say who does what, and by when.
tips: We will have the report carried out this week and the opinion letter issued by Friday.
I'll set out the conditions in a timeline and send it today.
